title: Commercial Lead - Clinical Trials
description: We’re Heidi. We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties. Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart. We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again. We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years. To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund. If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in. The role We are hiring a Clinical Trials Lead to own the commercial work that follows. You will develop Heidi’s view of the market, identify the strongest entry point, build senior relationships across the industry, secure early customers and shape a repeatable route to market. Your knowledge of clinical trials will inform and shape what Heidi builds. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who operates like a founder. You will make the calls, open the doors, write the proposal, run the meeting and stay accountable after the contract is signed. As the business proves itself, the role can grow into broader ownership of Heidi’s clinical trials business. What you’ll do Develop the market thesis. Map the clinical trials ecosystem, test the most valuable opportunities and recommend where Heidi should focus its time and capital. Lead customer development. Build direct relationships with senior decision makers across sponsors, biotechnology companies, CROs, sites and health systems. Conduct the outreach yourself and turn conversations into qualified opportunities. Own early commercial outcomes. Build the pipeline, secure design partners and paid programmes, and own early revenue. Define the measures that show whether the business is gaining traction. Shape the proposition. Turn buyer needs into a clear commercial offer, including target customer, value proposition, pricing, packaging and proof of value. Inform what Heidi builds. Bring evidence from customers and clinical trials workflows to the product lead. Help the team choose problems worth solving while the product lead retains ownership of product strategy and delivery. Navigate the buying process. Understand how life sciences organisations evaluate vendors, allocate budgets, manage procurement and compliance, and move from pilot to broader deployment. Build the delivery model. Work with product, engineering, clinical, legal and implementation colleagues to make early programmes successful and increasingly repeatable. Create the route to scale. Determine which partnerships, channels, proof points and team capabilities are required to grow beyond founder-led selling. Represent Heidi. Build Heidi’s credibility with customers, partners and industry networks through thoughtful engagement and useful domain expertise. What you’ll need The strongest candidates will combine deep clinical trials knowledge with a record of creating commercial value. We expect the following experience. Deep experience in the clinical trials industry through a pharmaceutical or biotechnology company, CRO, trial technology business, research network or closely related organisation. A strong understanding of how clinical trials are funded, sold, bought and delivered, including the incentives and constraints faced by sponsors, CROs and research sites. A record of building revenue, partnerships, a business line or a company in the sector. You can show what you personally originated and how it performed. Senior commercial credibility. You can open a conversation with an industry executive, diagnose the underlying business problem and move the relationship towards a concrete commitment. The judgement to operate in a regulated environment while respecting Good Clinical Practice, patient consent, privacy and data integrity. The independence to create structure, make decisions and produce results without an established playbook or a large supporting team. Passion for AI, shown through hands-on building, prototyping, or side projects. You default to building over requesting. You're confident in your thinking and open to being wrong. Great ideas win regardless of who surfaces them. How we show up Build for the next decade, not next quarter . Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism. Lead, don't wait . We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that. Follow the evidence . Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford. Own the outcome . Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander. Ship, measure, go again . A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless. Live in clinicians' reality . Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it. Why Heidi? You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver. Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally. We take care of you. title: Staff Engineer, EU Infrastructure
description: About Wolt At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe. Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life. About the Team Our Infrastructure teams build the foundation that engineers at Wolt, Deliveroo, and DoorDash build on: the compute, cloud, and networking capabilities that enable Engineering teams to develop, deploy, and run services at global scale. The EU Compute team has a specific focus on provisioning, scaling, and the efficient operation of GPU infrastructure for AI and ML workloads. This is an emerging space with plenty of greenfield opportunities. We're looking for a Staff Engineer to be a hands-on technical leader for this infrastructure work that crosses team and brand boundaries. You'll set direction for the platform, turn complex problems into deliverable plans, write and review production code, and help other engineers make sound decisions. It's an exciting time to join: we're building a global platform and the choices made now will shape how engineers across the company ship for years. What you'll be doing You'll own some of the hardest infrastructure problems in the company and make the platform easier to operate and safer to build on. We're determined to build great platform products and user experiences, and you'll be pivotal in making this reality. Day-to-day in this role you'll: Set technical direction for shared AWS and Kubernetes infrastructure, balancing reliability, security, developer experience, and cost. Lead substantial initiatives from design through rollout and operation, coordinating dependencies and decisions across Wolt, Deliveroo and DoorDash, focusing on workloads targeting GPUs. Evolve Kubernetes clusters, cloud networking, identity, and infrastructure provisioning to support growing and varied workloads. Build reusable Terraform patterns and self-service tooling that help teams provision infrastructure safely and consistently. Improve deployment and operational practices, including GitOps, observability, capacity planning, incident response and recovery. Use production signals and developer feedback to find platform friction, choose where to invest and measure whether changes actually help. Assist with supporting the platform, with deep focus on GPU infrastructure, as well as broad focus on compute in general. Gracefully sunset legacy infrastructure and tooling, and create strategies to reduce toil. Mentor engineers through design reviews, implementation and incidents, raising the quality of infrastructure work across teams. Our humble expectations Deep experience building and operating Kubernetes and AWS infrastructure in production. Familiarity with GPU workloads and orchestration is a plus. Strong software engineering skills: you use Go, Python or a similar language to build maintainable tools and automation. Experience with infrastructure as code (we use Terraform) and with designing systems that other engineering teams depend on. A track record of leading complex technical work across teams, including architectural decisions, delivery, and operational follow-through. You have the breadth to collaborate and design across team and domain boundaries, and the depth to have hands-on impact. Strong judgment on trade-offs in distributed systems, networking, security, reliability, and cloud cost. Clear communication, and the ability to bring people together around a practical technical direction. What we offer Scope and influence. Shape infrastructure used globally, while staying close to the engineering. Your work will help product teams ship services with greater ease and confidence. Real problems at global scale. Multi-cluster Kubernetes, AI / ML workloads, cloud networking, GitOps, and progressive delivery across a global company. Autonomy and ownership. Set direction and see it through from design to operation, with the backing of a global engineering organisation spanning Europe and the US. Growth. Room to expand your scope, whether through deeper technical leadership or broader cross-domain influence. Great people. Work with talented engineers and leaders in a diverse, international environment, mentoring and learning from others. Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel. title: Golang Backend Engineer, Financial Product Fraud
description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person. We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform. This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch. We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one. This role will be based in London , UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin. What you'll do: Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers. Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout. Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times. Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer. Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter. Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team. Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event. Our expectations: 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production. 1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly. A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one. Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar). Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability. Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality. Nice to have Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud. Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path. Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go. Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP). Experience working across multiple brands, regions, or regulatory regimes. What we value A product-oriented mindset. You think beyond the ticket, understand the "why" behind the work, and take a high level of responsibility for outcomes rather than output. Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new team on a new surface; parts of the charter are still being drawn, and you will help draw them. A track record of owning a project or feature end to end, especially in fast-paced environments. Clear and proactive communication, with a collaborative spirit. We work across three companies and several time zones, so we move fast, but we succeed together. An adversarial instinct. The best fraud engineers enjoy thinking like the attacker. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong. We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief. If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience. If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you! title: Field Marketing Manager - Net New EMEA (DAM)
description: About Us: At Sitecore, our mission is to simplify how brands reach, engage, and serve people by delivering intelligent, personalised digital experiences that connect the world. We empower the world’s most iconic brands to build lifelong relationships with their customers—seamlessly, smartly, and at scale. As the leading provider of agentic digital experience software, Sitecore brings together content, commerce, and data into one composable platform that enables brands to deliver millions of meaningful, adaptive experiences every day. Trusted by global leaders such as American Express, Porsche, Starbucks, and L’Oréal, Sitecore helps brands transform engagement through experiences that are not only personalised but predictive and dynamic. Our foundation is our people—a diverse, passionate, and collaborative global team spanning over 25 countries. We believe that every experience matters, and that belief starts with how we work together. Our values—empathy, accountability, clarity, and growth—guide how we lead, innovate, and connect. They are the behaviours that bring our mission and vision to life, every day, in every interaction. As we continue to evolve, we are actively cultivating AI skills across our teams to unlock new levels of creativity, efficiency, and insight. From engineering to customer experience, AI capabilities are becoming integral to how we design, build, and deliver the next generation of digital experiences. Learn more at Sitecore.com About the Role: Sitecore is seeking a dynamic and results-driven Field Marketing Manager to lead Net New demand generation for Digital Asset Management (DAM) across EMEA. This role will build market awareness, create qualified pipeline, and accelerate new customer acquisition through integrated field marketing aligned with regional go-to-market priorities. You will develop and execute multi-channel programs that bring the DAM value proposition to target accounts and priority industries. Working closely with the DAM team, regional sales, business development, product marketing, and campaigns, you will turn audience and market insight into measurable pipeline. The ideal candidate is entrepreneurial, commercially minded, data-driven, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. What You Will Do: Strategy & Planning Define and execute the Net New DAM demand generation strategy for EMEA, aligned with regional GTM, account priorities, and growth objectives Build integrated field marketing plans that increase DAM awareness, engage buying groups, and convert priority accounts Pipeline Generation Deliver qualified DAM pipeline targets alongside regional sales leadership, business development, and the DAM team Use account, intent, and market data to identify high-potential audiences, industries, and buying signals across EMEA Field Marketing Programs Design and deliver high-impact regional programs aligned with sales priorities, target account needs, and local market opportunities Create connected journeys across events, digital activation, executive engagement, and sales follow-up to move accounts through the funnel Campaign Execution Localize and activate global DAM campaigns, adapting the value proposition, messaging, content, and tactics for EMEA audiences Own the execution of field events, webinars, executive programs, and digital campaigns that support Net New DAM acquisition Performance & Optimization Track and report campaign engagement, sourced and resources Act as a trusted marketing advisor to sales teams, equipping them with DAM messaging, campaign plays, and timely follow-up guidance What You Need to Succeed: A minimum of 5 years of B2B marketing experience, ideally in SaaS, enterprise software, digital experience, content operations, or DAM Proven success in field marketing with responsibility for Net New pipeline creation across programs that engage target accounts and accelerate pipeline; DAM or content technology experience is advantageous Excellent communication, program management, and stakeholder management skills across Our culture is what makes that possible: we play to win, we obsess over quality, and we win as One Moss, and it works. Moss closed a €35 million Series C in August 2026, crossing a €1 billion valuation, and became one of Europe's fintech unicorns. Join us for what's next. London, UK Moss is building its strategic partnerships function from scratch, and this is one of the first two hires shaping it. You'll take target platforms from zero relationship to live, revenue-generating integration, owning the sourcing, business case, and delivery for each one. This is a build phase: you'll define your own playbook rather than follow one. You'll report to the Senior Director Partnerships and work closely with Product and Engineering on integration scope, and with the Channel team where partnerships overlap with existing ERP integrators. Your responsibilities Source and build strategic partnerships from scratch, identifying platforms that fit Moss's customer base and growth priorities Navigate complex partner organisations to reach the right decision makers, from founders and C-level contacts at smaller platforms to Heads of Partnerships at larger ones Build the commercial and technical case for each partnership and secure buy-in from both Moss leadership and the partner's stakeholders Own each partnership end-to-end, from an initial referral or lightweight integration through to a live, revenue-generating relationship Partner with Product and Engineering to scope integration requirements and manage delivery against Moss's API and roadmap Collaborate with the Channel team where accounting-platform integrators already exist, to avoid overlap and align on commercialisation Define and adjust your own playbook, prioritising partners by revenue potential and strategic fit as the market picture sharpens About you 5+ years in business development or partnerships within B2B SaaS, fintech, cloud, or payments At least 2 years specifically in strategic partnerships or integration-led partner roles, having built relationships from scratch rather than managed an existing book Working knowledge of APIs and how software platforms integrate with external partner systems In addition, here are the skills and attributes we are looking for: Thrives with full ownership of a plan and pipeline, without needing day-to-day direction Brings structure to ambiguous, still-being-built processes and partnerships Communicates progress, blockers, and trade-offs clearly across product, engineering, and leadership Balances ambition with realism, adjusting timelines to partner readiness and internal constraints without losing momentum About Moss Moss is the Finance AI platform for Europe's mid-sized businesses, giving companies real-time visibility and full control over their spend. By automating card issuing, invoice management and expenses, Moss simplifies financial workflows and frees finance and accounting teams from manual, administrative work. Founded in Berlin and used by more than 10,000 businesses including Flink, Schufa, n8n and Auto1, Moss has raised €220+ million to date and operates in Germany, the Netherlands, the UK and further EU markets. In August 2026, Moss closed a €35 million Series C led by Portage, crossing a €1 billion valuation and becoming one of Europe's newest fintech unicorns. Moss is backed by investors including Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Global Founders Capital, Cherry Ventures, A-Star. We're a team of 300+ people from 50+ nationalities across 5 offices in Europe and we hire, reward, and grow people based on Moss DNA : playing to win, obsessing over quality, winning as One Moss. If that's how you want to work, we want to hear from you. - here's what else to expect: Top-of-market compensation package, including equity. Our vibrant offices are at the heart of our culture, where in-person time fuels collaboration and connection over weekly breakfasts and Friday demos. Unless stated otherwise, benefits apply to full-time positions (interns and working students receive a tailored package). title: Data Privacy Analyst - Regulatory Compliance
description: The company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are. That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed. We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive. The team The Compliance team’s mission is to keep iwoca a safe and trusted lender for UK small businesses, and to make the compliant path the easy path for the teams we work with. We make sure iwoca meets its regulatory obligations, particularly the financial crime, sanctions and data protection requirements that apply across our suite of products and services. We are the second line of defence for the UK business. We advise the people building and running the business on what the rules require, set the policies and standards they work to, and test whether what happens in practice matches them. We work alongside the product teams so that each product meets its obligations and can grow. Data protection is central to what we do. We hold the data privacy function for the UK business and own how iwoca handles personal data end to end: the lawful basis for how customer, applicant and third-party data is used; data subject access requests and other individual rights; personal data breaches; retention and deletion; records of processing; marketing and consent; the privacy review of new products and features; and the governance of automated decisioning and AI tooling. How we work: We enable rather than block. The answer is rarely just “no” — it’s what it would take to get to yes, and what the firm is accepting if it goes ahead anyway. We go to the source. Positions are grounded in the actual rule, regulation or guidance, and we can show where they come from. We’re proportionate. Controls match the risk in front of us. We don’t build process for its own sake. We’re close to the business. We work directly with Tech, Data, Credit, Operations and Legal, and we want to be in the room early rather than at the end. The role As Data Privacy Analyst you will run iwoca’s day-to-day UK data protection work and help the business apply UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR in practice. Your primary focus will be the statutory core: data subject access requests, data protection impact assessments, legitimate interests assessments, personal data breaches and records of processing. The role is not only to run that work but to improve it. A significant part of the job is identifying where our privacy operations could be automated, supported by AI or otherwise improved, assessing what each option would take and what it would mean for compliance, and specifying it well enough for our Tech and Data teams to deliver. There is real room for the role to grow: as you build credibility, so does the scope, towards owning areas of the framework outright, leading on AI and automation governance, and taking a larger advisory remit across the business. You will report to the Data Privacy Manager and work closely with the Head of Compliance who also acts as iwoca’s DPO, so you will have experienced support on the harder judgement calls. This is a hands-on role and the work is visible — much of it goes to senior stakeholders or to the regulator. Impact and influence Individual rights and data breaches. Own data subject access requests from intake to response — scoping the search, applying exemptions and meeting the statutory deadline — along with erasure, rectification and objection requests. Triage and investigate suspected personal data breaches, assess them against the 72-hour notification test, and keep the breach register accurate. Privacy assessments and advice. Assist with DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments and other privacy reviews on new products, features, suppliers and data flows. Be an accessible first point of contact for teams across iwoca with a data protection question, and give them an answer they can act on, early enough to shape what they build. Records, policies and reporting. Keep the record of processing activities accurate as the business changes, hold the retention and deletion schedules to account, review data processing agreements with suppliers, help maintain our data protection policies and standards, and produce the privacy reporting that goes to senior stakeholders. AI and automated decisioning. Help assess AI tooling and automated decision-making across lending and operations: what personal data goes in, what lawful basis supports it, what the model does with it, and what rights customers have over the outcome. That includes the risks specific to these systems — decisions taken without meaningful human involvement, bias in outcomes, unreliable model output — and recommending how we address them. Automation and improvement. Identify the manual steps in our privacy operations that should not be manual, assess the options, and set out the requirements and compliance implications clearly enough for Tech and Data to deliver them. The requirements Essential skills Experience. Experience in data protection or privacy operations, or in a compliance, legal, risk or operational role where data protection was a real part of the job. Data protection knowledge. A solid practical understanding of UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR, and of how the ICO expects firms to apply them. Familiarity with the changes made by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 is an advantage. Privacy operations and assessments. Hands-on experience of statutory work: DSARs, DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments, breach handling, ROPA maintenance or data processing agreement review. You may not have done all of these — but we want to see that you have done some of them properly. AI and automation. A real interest in, and working understanding of, how data protection law applies to AI and automated decision-making. Enough technical fluency to see where a manual process could be automated, set out what is needed, and hold your own in a conversation with engineers. Stakeholder management: Comfortable dealing directly with product, engineering, marketing, credit and operations teams, and able to give a non-specialist a clear answer they can act on rather than a legal summary. Bonus: Sector experience. Financial services or fintech, ideally in lending or payments. Credentials. A privacy or AI qualification such as CIPP/E, CIPM, or ICO-recognised practitioner certificates — or working towards one. Practical tooling. Experience using Claude Code, LLMs or privacy management platforms. The culture At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time. The offices We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work: Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks. Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions. The benefits Flexible working hours. Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership. A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses. A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents. 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave. A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years. Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support. 3% Pension contributions on total earnings. An employee equity incentive scheme. Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money. Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme. Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield. And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer: A learning and development budget for everyone. Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers. Access to learning platforms like Treehouse. Our comms function works across the business to position iwoca as a leading voice in SME finance. You'll collaborate closely with Product, Commercial, and Executive teams to translate business priorities into compelling narratives that drive both brand awareness and customer acquisition. You'll also help with the BAU media activities that keep iwoca front-of-mind with key journalists and stakeholders. Examples of the type of work you'll be doing: 1. SME survey research: Twice a year you'll help commission original survey research, working with established research partners to design questionnaires capturing timely SME sentiment. For each product, you'll get under the hood with the Venture Leads - understanding commercial objectives, customer pain points, competitive landscape - then translating that into comms plans that drive both coverage and business outcomes. You'll own two products, with the split decided once you're in the job. 3. Support our public affairs and policy work iwoca works with government and policymakers to make the case for better access to finance for small businesses. You'll support this work, engaging with relevant government departments, industry bodies and ministers where relevant. This could include: Tracking policy and regulatory developments that affect SMEs and SME lending. Helping draft consultation responses, policy briefings and position papers. Using our lending and survey data to build the evidence behind our policy positions. Preparing briefing materials for meetings with officials, industry bodies and ministers. The requirements Essential: Up to two years' experience in communications, PR, public affairs, policy, journalism or a related field. Internships and placements count, and we welcome recent graduates. Excellent writing skills with the ability to craft data-driven stories, press releases, briefing materials, and media pitches that cut through. Ability to work at pace across multiple projects simultaneously, with strong organisational skills. You'll need to be confident managing and analysing data with either Excel or Google Sheets. Experience in public affairs, policy or government relations, or an understanding of how policy is made. Any exposure to product launches or translating complex propositions into accessible narratives. Experience pitching to journalists or securing coverage in relevant press. Comfortable working with senior stakeholders. Commercial awareness and understanding of what drives media coverage in fintech and SME finance. title: Fitness Director, Women's Health (12 Month FTC)
description: <p><em>We are the UK's leading premium publisher, home to iconic and influential media brands including Esquire, Men's & Women's Health, ELLE, Good Housekeeping, Harper's Bazaar, Digital Spy, Cosmopolitan, Red and more. At Hearst UK, we don't just create content – we shape culture.</em></p> <p><em>Our workplace is driven by passion, shaped by authenticity and powered by creativity. We back bold ideas, act with an entrepreneurial mindset and continually evolve to meet the moment - while respecting the legacy that's brought us here. We believe in each other's potential and push boundaries together to create meaningful impact, both across the media landscape and in people's lives.</em></p> <p><em>We're proud of our heritage - but even more excited about making history.</em></p> <p><em>Hearst UK operates an in-office policy with flexible Fridays. Our office is based at <strong>House of Hearst, 30 Panton Street, St James's, London, SW1Y 4AJ</strong>, where teams collaborate in person and connect across brands and functions.</em></p> <p><strong><em>Salary - £50,000 - £55,000 - Salary is dependent on experience and will be assessed in line with the candidate’s skills, knowledge, and relevant expertise.</em></strong></p> <h3><strong>The Role…</strong></h3> <p>As the Fitness Director, you will lead the strategy and delivery of Women’s Health’s fitness content across all platforms, including membership, digital, print, video, social and events.</p> <p>Working closely with the Editor-in-chief, wider Women’s Health team, Hearst commercial team, central app leads, fitness professionals and PRs, you’ll develop compelling editorial content to the highest possible standard.</p> <p>You’ll also line manage two junior fitness writers and act as an ambassador for Women’s Health, Hearst UK and its values.</p> <p><strong>Main Duties…</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead on the brand’s fitness content strategy across the website, approving daily agenda-setting ideas from two junior fitness writers, ensuring content is legally sound, in line with the brand’s stance on fitness, produced to the highest possible editorial standard, and delivered in line with deadlines.</li> <li>Produce multiple agenda-setting digital ideas of your own each day, optimised for SEO, Google Discover and trending news, to power womenshealthmag.com.uk’s biggest traffic vertical: fitness.</li> <li>Line manage two junior fitness writers, approving and feeding back on multiplatform pitches on a daily basis, and report on digital fitness performance on a weekly basis.</li> <li>Work closely with the brand’s social media team to lead on WH’s fitness social media strategy, while owning all fitness content in print and working with the Editor to flatplan, create and commission timely fitness features for 10 monthly issues.</li> <li>Own fitness membership content, creating two monthly members-only training plans, and lead on WH’s video fitness strategy, prioritising members-only app content to produce in-house real-time workout videos.</li> <li>Lead on Women’s Health’s annual Fit Night Out event and additional members-only fitness events, working with events teams to plan and coordinate workouts, panels and ticket promotion, while meeting commercial sponsorship briefs.</li> <li>Commission and edit agenda-setting freelance fitness features for both digital and print platforms, assist the editor with production of fitness bookazines and supplements, and act as an ambassador for the brand, Hearst UK, and its values, through media and public appearances.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What We Are Looking For…</strong></p> <ul> <li>A fitness specialist with experience leading on fitness content strategy across digital platforms.</li> <li>Experience producing agenda-setting digital ideas, optimised for SEO, Google Discover and trending news.</li> <li>Experience line managing writers, approving pitches and providing feedback on multiplatform content.</li> <li>Experience creating and commissioning high-quality fitness features for digital and print platforms.</li> <li>Experience working across social media, video, membership content and events.</li> <li>Experience working with internal teams, external fitness professionals, PRs, commercial teams and app leads.</li> <li>The ability to act as an ambassador for the brand, Hearst UK, and its values, through media and public appearances.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Benefits…</strong></p> <p>(Your benefits at Hearst UK are more than just extras - they are tools to help you thrive in every part of life.)</p> <p><strong>Hearst Exclusives - Only for You!</strong></p> <ul> <li>Get adventurous with Good Housekeeping Taste and Beauty Testing Panels - yes, you could be trying the next big thing in beauty, food & drink.</li> <li>Snag luxe beauty steals at our legendary office sample sales - score big on top brands without breaking the bank!</li> </ul> <p><strong>Inclusion, Health & Wellbeing: Feel Your Best</strong></p> <ul> <li>Stay healthy with Specsavers eye care, a company-funded Health Cash Plan, and access to mental health support.</li> <li>Get active and stress-free with discounted gym memberships and the Cycle to Work scheme.</li> <li>Embrace flexibility with a Location Flex and Holiday Exchange to take time when you need it.</li> <li>Take time to give back with a Charity Day and access wellbeing resources whenever you need them.</li> <li>Join one of our Hearst ERG Groups.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Financial Wellness - Boost Your Budget</strong></p> <ul> <li>Plan ahead with a generous Workplace Pension, Income Protection, Life Assurance and Season Ticket Loan for easier commuting.</li> <li>Make smarter money moves using Salary Finance tools, Financial Wellbeing sessions, and Home Tech benefits to spread costs.</li> <li>Treat yourself with major discounts across London plus everyday savings via the HAPI at Hearst app.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Hearst UK is deeply committed to using our influential brands to reflect the world we want to live in – one that respects, protects, represents and uplifts the voices and opinions of all people. As a business, we recognise the significant benefits of creativity, collaboration and innovation that comes with diverse teams. Not only is diversifying the voices in our organization the right thing to do, but it also helps us to make powerful and exciting content that can be enjoyed by many more people. This is why we’re working to build a sense of true belonging within our business and foster a culture in which everyone feels heard.</strong></p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Software Engineer, Enterprise
description: <div> <p>At Scale AI, we’re not just building AI tools—we’re pioneering the next era of enterprise AI. In this role, you’ll build the core infrastructure that powers AI products for some of the world’s largest enterprises—designing scalable APIs, distributed data systems, and robust deployment pipelines that enable production-grade reliability and performance. </p> <p>This is a rare opportunity to be at the center of the GenAI revolution, solving hard backend and infrastructure challenges that make AI truly work at enterprise scale. title: Senior Applied Researcher
description: <div class="content-intro"><div> <div> <div class="gmail_quote"> <div> <div><span id="m_-113912706363268805m_-2746164444908759431gmail-docs-internal-guid-131e4fb0-7fff-b4e9-ff50-e8cf32449b1b">CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at <a href="https://www.coreweave.com">www.coreweave.com</a>.</span></div> <div> </div> <div>We're proud to be a Living Wage accredited Employer.</div> </div> </div> </div> </div> <p> </p></div><p><strong>What You’ll Do:</strong></p> <p>CoreWeave’s Physical AI team is building the essential cloud platform for AI innovators, applying machine learning to solve intractable physics and engineering challenges. We operate at the intersection of advanced cloud infrastructure and applied data science, transforming how complex industrial products - such as automotive systems, aircraft, and advanced batteries - are conceived, tested, and developed.</p> <p><strong>About the role:</strong></p> <p>As an Applied Researcher, you will help solve machine learning problems across the Physical AI space. This is a hands-on role for someone with a strong technical foundation and a generalist mindset who wants to contribute across problem framing, experimentation, deployment, and ongoing support, with guidance from experienced researchers and engineers.</p> <p>You will work closely with engineering, product, and client-facing teams to turn advanced ML methods into production-ready solutions that can be trusted in real customer environments. The role blends applied research with practical delivery, and requires someone who can work collaboratively, surface risks and limitations, and communicate technical decisions clearly.</p> <p><strong>Who You Are:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience in data science, machine learning, or applied AI, gained through industry roles, applied research, or a combination of both, with evidence of applying ML to practical problems.</li> <li>Strong programming skills in Python, with practical experience using scientific computing and ML libraries such as NumPy, pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, or TensorFlow.</li> <li>Experience contributing to the deployment or support of ML systems, or a good understanding of how models move from experimentation into production, including cloud-based environments.</li> <li>Strong grounding in statistical modelling, machine learning experimentation, and evaluation.</li> <li>Experience working with time-series, high-dimensional, or imperfect real-world datasets.</li> <li>Strong technical curiosity and a habit of keeping up with current ML and AI research.</li> <li>Comfortable working cross-functionally with engineering, product, and customer-facing teams, and able to explain technical decisions clearly to different audiences.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Preferred: (if applicable)</strong></p> <ul> <li>Background in engineering, physics, chemistry, or another STEM discipline connected to complex physical systems.</li> <li>Experience with anomaly detection, optimisation, reliability-focused modelling, or related approaches in industrial settings.</li> <li>Experience building or experimenting with agents or autonomous systems.</li> <li>Familiarity with MLOps, model monitoring, and efficient compute practices.</li> <li>Experience working with sparse, noisy, or imperfect real-world data from labs, heavy industry, or other applied environments.</li> <li>Track record of collaborating closely with deployed or client-facing teams to bring advanced methods into operational use.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Wondering if you’re a good fit? We believe in investing in our people, and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams - even if you aren't a 100% skill or experience match. description: <div> <p><strong>Weekly office requirement: </strong>2 days per week, Mondays & Wednesdays<br><strong>Employment type:</strong> Permanent<br><strong>Seniority level:</strong> Senior<br><strong>Language:</strong> All stages of the recruitment process will be conducted in English</p> </div> <p>At GWI we’re always looking for extraordinary people who thrive on making an extraordinary impact. It could be the start of something, well, extraordinary.</p> <p> </p> <h1>Sounds great, what will I be doing? 🤔</h1> <p>As our Senior Product Manager you’ll own a new suite of AI and ML-powered data products at the forefront of innovation in the market research industry. This is a chance to shape how businesses around the world access and act on consumer insight, and to define what AI-native market research looks like rather than follow someone else’s lead.</p> <p>You’ll set the vision and strategy for the suite, turn it into a roadmap, and lead the squad that builds it. You’ll work closely with Data Science, ML and Engineering, as well as Design, Sales, Client Success, Marketing and Finance, with plenty of direct contact with clients and prospects.</p> <p>A few things you’ll be responsible for:</p> <p>👉 Defining the vision, strategy, and positioning of our new AI and data product suite, and how it fits into GWI’s wider platform</p> <p>👉 Identifying where AI and ML create real value for clients, and separating what’s genuinely useful from what’s just novel</p> <p>👉 Working with Data Science and ML Engineering on the models, data, pipelines and methodology behind the products, so they are accurate, reliable, scalable, and trusted</p> <p>👉 Defining how we measure AI quality, including evaluation frameworks, accuracy and reliability benchmarks, and feedback loops, and deciding what “good enough to ship” means</p> <p>👉 Shaping our approach to responsible AI, covering transparency, data governance, privacy and explainability, so clients can trust what the products tell them</p> <p>👉 Building the roadmap from client feedback, market and competitor insight, internal stakeholder input and usage analytics, then prioritising the most valuable work</p> <p>👉 Taking products from early discovery and prototyping through to launch and adoption, including shaping the commercial model, pricing and packaging with Finance and Revenue teams (including usage-based and consumption models)</p> <p>👉 Communicating progress, trade-offs and results clearly to the Exec team and wider business</p> <p>It’s also fun. Shaking things up is what working for GWI is all about. In a fast-moving AI landscape, you’ll need to be flexible, comfortable with continuous change, and happy working in a high-tempo environment.</p> <h1>What do I need to bring with me? 🧳</h1> <p>You’ll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires. You don’t have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you’re willing to learn. Here’s what the team will be looking for in you:</p> <p>👉 You’ve shipped AI, ML, data or analytics products at a B2B company, ideally SaaS</p> <p>👉 You understand how AI and ML products are built (for example, LLMs, retrieval, agents, predictive models) </p> <p>👉 You’re comfortable with data. You can work with engineers on data quality, modelling, and delivery (APIs, dashboards, integrations)</p> <p>👉 You’ve built complex roadmaps with cross-functional dependencies, and you can balance multiple priorities without losing the plot</p> <p>👉 You make informed decisions at pace, even when the picture isn’t complete, and you’re happy taking a big initiative and running with it</p> <p>👉 You’re a strong problem solver, negotiator, and influencer. You get alignment without needing authority</p> <p>👉 You explain complex things clearly to very different audiences: execs, engineers, customers</p> <p>👉 You ask questions and draw knowledge out of your team to find the right engineering, data science and design solutions</p> <p>👉 Bonus points if you’ve worked in market research, consumer insight or analytics, with large-scale survey or behavioural datasets, or on usage-based pricing for AI or API products</p> <p>Equally important is attitude. We want people who think big (to make an impact), ask why (to find a better way), and show respect (to everyone, at every level, all the time). Those are our values, and they’re a big part of what we’re looking for in you.</p> <p> </p> <h1>Why Join Us</h1> <p>👉 You’ll work on a new AI-powered product suite at the leading edge of the market research industry</p> <p>👉 You’ll build on GWI’s large-scale consumer datasets, a strong foundation for AI products that competitors can’t easily replicate</p> <p>👉 You’ll have room to shape the strategy and run your own squad your way<br><br><br></p> <h1>What We Offer 🧘</h1> <p>At GWI, you’ll find meaningful work, visible impact, and a culture that empowers you to do your best. Our package includes:</p> <ul> <li>Time to recharge – 25 days’ annual leave, plus office closures over the holidays.</li> <li>Health & wellbeing – Health cash plan, enhanced family benefits, carer days, and mental health support.</li> <li>Financial benefits – Competitive salary, 4% pension matching, and recognition programs that celebrate success.</li> <li>Flexibility & balance – Flexitime, early Friday finishes, hybrid and remote options, plus a “work from home” budget.</li> <li>Career growth – Accredited learning, leadership development, and global career mobility.</li> <li>Community & impact – DE&I initiatives, volunteering opportunities, donation matching, and payroll giving.</li> </ul> <p>Put all that together and GWI is the friendliest, most fulfilling place any of us has ever worked.</p> <h1>Diversity, Equity & Inclusion 🫶</h1> <p>Diversity is fundamental to who we are—as a data company and as a workplace. Our data reflects global realities, and so must our teams. We strive to build a workforce as diverse and inclusive as the insights we deliver.</p> <p>As a Disability Confident employer, we welcome applications from disabled candidates and are committed to making adjustments throughout the hiring process—whether that's extra time, materials in advance or a different format, breaks, an adjusted interview format, assistive tools, or flexible scheduling. We're happy to discuss whatever would work best for you.</p> <p>We actively encourage applications from underrepresented and marginalised communities.</p> <p>At GWI, you'll find a place to contribute meaningfully, grow professionally, and belong fully.</p> <p> </p> <p><iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/2g0akAyAlUU?si=dIgYyrKaAlNZK-NQ" width="560" height="314"></iframe></p> <p>#li-hybrid<br>#LI-LV1</p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Strategic Account Executive (UK)

We're on the frontier of an entirely new category: Agentic AI. We enable enterprises to build high-performing hybrid workforces made up of both humans and AI agents. These AI agents aren't generic copilots. They're fully trained digital teammates that learn from your best people, your content, and your business strategy—ready to get to work from day one. Our platform combines generative AI, human-in-the-loop workflows, and a living Enterprise Skill Graph that continuously learns and improves. Whether you're launching a product globally, onboarding new hires, translating learning content, or aligning legal teams across regions, Smartcat turns knowledge into action and action into scale. Over 1,000 companies, including 20% of the Fortune 500, rely on Smartcat to bring their business to the world—instantly, accurately, and in every language. As a Series C company with consistently high year-over-year growth, we're scaling fast and investing in people who want to shape the future of work with us. Join us in unlocking global potential, one human and agent team at a time. WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN OUR TEAM You'll be a strategic revenue owner on a Tier-1, board-level seat — building multi-million ARR relationships across Smartcat's highest-potential enterprise customers, with direct access to leadership and hands-on coaching from a CRO who previously scaled a company to $150M+ ARR through a successful exit. This is a real business bet: deep cross-functional support across Product, FDE, CX, Marketing, and RevOps, in exchange for elite performance and elite character. OUTCOMES Own Expansion ARR and NRR across a defined portfolio of enterprise accounts, building and executing a clear plan to multi-million ARR per account cluster Proactively source upsell, HOW YOU'LL RAMP By Day 30: Learn Smartcat's agentic platform, Multi-Agent Systems, and AI/governance value story in depth Get up to speed on your account portfolio: current relationships, whitespace, buying centers, and expansion potential Build working relationships with your Forward Deployed Engineer, Customer AI Engineer, Product, Marketing, and RevOps partners By Day 60: Be leading executive-level conversations independently around AI value, ROI, and outcomes Have identified and begun pursuing specific upsell, cross-sell, and expansion opportunities across your portfolio Have a shortlist of new enterprise logo targets with a clear rationale for long-term ARR potential By Day 90: Be executing a clear, account-cluster-level plan toward multi-million ARR, with active expansion motions underway Be multi-threaded across business, technical, and finance/procurement stakeholders in your top accounts Own an accurate, rigorous forecast with risk called early and clearly WHAT YOU'VE ACCOMPLISHED A validated track record of quotas and performance history, with references that hold up to scrutiny Sustained performance over time across roles — including how you've learned from losses, not just wins Demonstrated fluency across modern enterprise sales approaches (Challenger, value-based selling, MEDDPICC, consultative/executive narrative selling), applied situationally rather than dogmatically Experience navigating complex enterprise organizations — procurement, legal, security, and governance reviews — to reach real decision-makers A track record operating with humility as a force multiplier: confident without ego, coachable, quick to share credit, focused on outcomes over recognition Comfort delivering uncomfortable truth — challenging customers, disqualifying weak opportunities, calling risk early with data and conviction Why joining Smartcat might be your best move so far A global, connected team We're a team of 200+ people across 30+ countries, working together through a hub-and-spoke model anchored in eight key locations: New York, London, Lisbon, Costa Rica, Serbia, Armenia, Georgia, and Spain. Most of our roles are remote-friendly, giving you the flexibility to do your best work from where you thrive. For customer-facing teams, we prioritize proximity to our customers, ensuring we stay deeply connected to their needs and deliver an exceptional experience. No matter where you're based, you'll be part of a highly collaborative, globally-distributed team that values ownership, speed, and meaningful impact. Be part of an AI Native Organization We are highly innovative, using AI across all areas of the organization to accelerate decision-making and free people to focus on strategy and high-impact work. We embrace new ideas and encourage all Smartcaters, regardless of level or department, to manage their own AI Agents. At Smartcat you'll shape how AI transforms the workplace and play an integral role in ensuring Smartcat remains a leader in AI innovation. Innovating a $100 Billion industry Smartcat is reshaping the $100B multilingual content industry with an AI-powered platform that makes it easy for companies to create, translate, and localize global content at scale. Our platform enables enterprise teams to move away from slow, traditional outsourcing methods, and achieve fast, high-quality results, at a fraction of the cost. Join the rocketship to scale-up 10x and beyond together We are looking for someone to become an integral part of our team and play a crucial role in the most exciting part of our journey: transitioning from a post-Series C startup to a company exceeding $100M in ARR and $1B in valuation. Our journey isn't for the faint of heart. We are growing at 130% YoY, thanks to our strong product-market fit and high-performing team, and plan to accelerate from here. title: Engineering Manager – Server-Driven UI (Codeless)
description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. About the role We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead Codeless, our internal Server-Driven UI (SDUI) platform team. In this role, you will lead a cross-functional team bridging mobile/web frontend engineering and core platform backend systems. While this role is deeply rooted in modern UI architecture, its mission goes beyond standard UI development: Codeless empowers product teams across the organization to ship dynamic, native UI experiences dynamically from the backend—eliminating app store release bottlenecks, dramatically accelerating feature iteration, and establishing a unified UI schema across iOS, Android, and Web. What you'll be doing This is a role with broad impact, from hands-on technical guidance to championing web and mobile accessibility across the company. We're looking for a leader who excels at fostering collaboration and can confidently guide a concept from initial idea to robust implementation. Day-to-day in this role you'll: Team Leadership & Strategy: Build, mentor, and scale an engineering team responsible for our core Server-Driven UI platform ("Codeless"). Foster an inclusive, high-ownership engineering culture. Platform Architecture & Evolution: Oversee the design and evolution of dynamic layout engines, declarative UI schemas, and client rendering frameworks across iOS, Android, and Web. Developer Velocity & Platform Adoption: Partner with product feature teams to drive internal adoption of Codeless. Ensure the platform provides exceptional Developer Experience, clear tooling, robust design system integration, and seamless debugging workflows. Technical Execution & Quality: Set high technical standards for platform performance, payload optimization, caching strategies, backward compatibility, and graceful offline/fallback behavior across client devices. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Product Managers, Design System leaders, and Core Infrastructure engineers to align the Codeless roadmap with broader company initiatives and global design paradigms. What you'll need to thrive Engineering Management: 3+ years of experience managing software engineering teams, with a track record of coaching engineers, delivering complex platform initiatives, and driving technical strategy. UI & Platform Domain Expertise: Strong foundational background in mobile (iOS/Android) or modern web architecture (React, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, or declarative UI paradigms). Product & Platform Mindset: Ability to treat internal product engineering teams as customers, evaluating platform success through developer velocity, adoption metrics, and rendering performance. Why join us At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters—solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving. We're food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to: 🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day. 🌱 See your impact, fast Ship, test and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership environment. 🧠 Grow through challenge and ownership Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support. 🌎 A culture built for builders High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning. 💰 Share in the success you help create Competitive salary and equity options, so you're rewarded for the impact you make. ➡️ Want a deeper look at how we build? Check out our Tech Blog. We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Explore our Engineering Interview Guide here to help you feel confident at each stage. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong. We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief. If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience. If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you! Beware of recruitment scams: DASH Brands will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about DASH Brands' legitimate recruiting process at careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness . title: Engineering Intern (London, Summer 2027)
description: About Hiya At Hiya, we’re making business calls more trusted, useful, and effective. Voice remains one of the most important ways businesses communicate with their customers, but the value of a call depends on trust. When customers do not recognize who is calling or why, important conversations are missed, customer relationships suffer, and business outcomes are harder to achieve. Hiya helps businesses create trusted calling experiences that benefit both sides of the conversation: enterprises can reach customers with confidence, and customers can answer with confidence. Our products support branded business calling, trusted caller identity, call performance insights, customer engagement, and voice security capabilities that help businesses strengthen relationships and improve outcomes. This role sits in a core business area for Hiya and is focused on helping SMB and enterprise customers succeed. About the Role The engineering intern position is for an individual contributor who is responsible for architecting, implementing, and maintaining significant systems that serve hundreds of millions of requests per month. Hiya provides high-availability, latency-sensitive capabilities to telecoms, mobile apps, and other partners. In addition, you'll work with engineering teams across Hiya, some in Seattle and some in Europe, to define and deliver shared components and services. From day one, you will be paired with a dedicated mentor who provides structured guidance, technical feedback, and ongoing career mentorship. What You'll Do Design, code, and operate high-performance services and data processing pipelines on a modern technology stack, supported by a structured technical crash course during your first two weeks covering our core tools, architecture, and repositories. Work at a supportive and fast-growing startup with a fantastic team, where you can collaborate with and learn from other great team members. Make an impact in the lives of hundreds of millions of consumers. Be supported in developing your skills and accelerating your career. What We Are Looking For Engineering: CS majors - 2nd year (graduating 2028) Excitement to work on innovative technology advancements A philosophy of iteration and continuous improvement Working knowledge of building services that adhere to operational SLAs A preference for velocity over perfection A commitment to respectful and impactful collaboration Self-motivated and excited to learn about new technologies Our Interview Process: The Hiya Voice AI Challenge Once we’ve confirmed your eligibility, you’ll receive the Hiya Voice AI Challenge by email-- a chance to build a working prototype of a voice-driven product in one of five tracks: Accessibility, Productivity, Creative Voice, Security, or Real-Time Assistance. You’ll have one week to build it, with optional virtual office hours along the way if you’d like to pitch your idea and get steering from our team first. From there: Submit and get reviewed. One of our engineers reviews your work. If we’d like to explore your project further, you’ll get a link to book a 30-minute virtual session with an engineer or two-- a quick demo, a walkthrough of your code, and some questions. Final interviews, in person at Hiya. Candidates who advance join us for a final round in London ( 2nd & 3rd of December) : a debugging/fixing session, a chance to add a feature to your own project, and a conversation about Hiya’s values. AI tools are welcome and encouraged the whole way through. What You Can Expect From Us Dedicated technical mentorship with structured, regular feedback check-ins Clear project scope and goals provided right at the start of your internship Comprehensive onboarding to get you up to speed on Hiya's tooling, codebases, and systems quickly A supportive, collaborative environment built on psychological safety and genuine impact How We Work Hiya is not a passive environment. We expect people to take ownership, form opinions, and engage directly with hard problems. We work with a high degree of transparency and autonomy . Context is shared openly, and decisions are discussed, challenged, and then made. Once a call is made, we commit and move forward. You'll be expected to work through ambiguity, weigh tradeoffs, and take responsibility for results, while keeping a high bar for quality and customer trust. Every team member at Hiya is expected to live our core values: Serve, our customers and partners by holding a high bar for trust and quality Own, share in success and open up to failures Lead, listen, show up with a point of view but commit entirely once a decision has been made Improve, even if it means changing course or contradicting ourselves Do, rather than observe Come Work With Us! We're building a team with diverse perspectives, identities, and professional experiences. We evaluate candidates through a business lens and believe that diversity and unique viewpoints make our company stronger, more dynamic, and a great place to build a career. We've been recognized by Built In, GeekWire, Comparably, G2, Forbes, and Deloitte Technology Fast 500 for our culture, innovation, leadership, compensation, and more. At Hiya, we're a people-centric company focused on helping each employee grow both personally and professionally. We create a culture of support and empowerment that challenges the status quo, resulting in an energized team that's passionate about their work. You'll love working here if you're looking for an innovative challenge that's disrupting an industry. Come join us! Hiya is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to building an inclusive environment for all employees. Compensation: £45K • £45,000 Annual-equivalent, pro-rated across 12 weeks, plus pension £45K Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow
